prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, opening the field of moire quantum matter.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B001 alone, with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. After the full first-round exchange the case rests on three things I weigh scientifically. First, the 2011 continuum model made a sharp, falsifiable statement (a magic twist angle at which the Dirac velocity vanishes and the bands flatten), and the 2018 experiments found correlated insulating and superconducting states in exactly that regime. Second, the existence of these phases has been reproduced by several independent groups and carried into twisted multilayers, moire transition-metal dichalcogenides and fractional Chern insulators, so the discovery does not depend on the open pairing mechanism. Third, the three-name set is accurate for the prediction (a joint two-author paper) and follows the group-leader convention on the experimental side. From my own field, what is unusual is that interaction strength is tuned by geometry and gate voltage rather than by chemistry, and a simple model anticipated it. The citation should be worded narrowly: it credits the flat-band prediction and the observation of the correlated and superconducting phases, and makes no claim about the origin of the superconductivity.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains timing and credit. The pairing mechanism and several correlated states are still debated, the field is moving quickly, and a prize now could freeze a narrative that later work refines. The three-name limit also leaves Cao (first author of the 2018 papers), Fatemi, and the confirming groups of Dean, Efetov, Young and Yazdani outside, and earlier twisted-graphene band-structure theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto, Suarez Morell) has a claim that careful citation wording only partly answers. Finally, B001 and B007 cannot be combined within three names, so choosing B001 means leaving a mature, cleanly attributed invention for another year. I judge these costs acceptable but real, and the experimental attribution is the weakest part of my own position.

responses.point: Kroll asked directly whether my fifth-place ranking of B007 reflects a bias toward discovery over enabling capability, or a specific attribution concern, and said that the clock has the same prediction-then-confirmation structure as B001.
responses.response: It is mostly a difference in what I weigh, and I accept that. I do not dispute that enabling new measurements is a legitimate and long-standing basis for the prize, and I do not have an attribution objection to the Katori-Ye pair itself. The structural analogy has force, but it is not identical: magic-wavelength trapping removes a known systematic error from an established clock scheme, whereas the flat-band prediction anticipated a new regime of correlated matter that no one had observed. My residual attribution worries concern credit for other Sr and Yb groups and ultrastable-laser work outside the two names, which I mentioned in round 1. So my gap between B001 and B007 is a judgment about field-opening novelty, not evidence that the clock is weaker, and I would not object strongly if the committee chose B007 on maturity grounds. I also agree with your point that the SI redefinition should not carry the argument either way.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that the lattice clock claim is a measured number reproduced in Tokyo, Boulder, Braunschweig and Paris, whereas the interpretation of the twisted-graphene phases is unstable, and she keeps B007 ahead partly because its attribution is clean and B001's is not.
responses.response: I agree that B007 is cleaner on attribution and that this is a real asymmetry. I disagree that the interpretation of B001 is unstable in the sense that matters for a citation. What the experiments established, the insulating and superconducting states near the magic angle, has been seen by independent groups in several device generations; what is open is why the material superconducts. A citation can be written to the first and silent on the second, much as the cuprate discovery was recognised before a mechanism existed. Your point about the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize is the strongest argument against B007 that I would take seriously, and you answer it well by treating the magic-wavelength lattice as a distinct trapping method; I accept that distinction. It narrows my reservation about B007 but does not change my first choice.

responses.point: Mehlig moved from a two-name to a three-name B001 and argues that waiting for a pairing mechanism would be a stricter standard than the committee has applied to other experimental discoveries.
responses.response: I agree with both parts. Dropping Bistritzer would break the logic of crediting the prediction at all, since the magic angle comes from the joint 2011 calculation, and with three places available no other name competes for that slot on the theory side. I also agree that requiring a settled mechanism is stricter than past practice. I would add one point on your own caution: it applies to our citation wording more than to the prize itself. The text should name the prediction and the observed phases and nothing about mechanism, which meets the concern you and Lindroth share without changing the configuration.

responses.point: Olsson places the real attribution risk on the theory side, where earlier twisted-graphene band-structure work exists, and argues the citation should name the continuum-model prediction of flat bands at magic angles rather than twisted graphene generally.
responses.response: I agree and have adopted that wording in my citation. Earlier work by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto and by Suarez Morell and colleagues established twist-dependent band reconstruction and Dirac-velocity renormalisation; what the 2011 paper added was the quantitative flat-band condition at a specific angle, which is what experiment tested. Where I differ slightly is on the experimental side: I treat the confirming groups as evidence of maturity, as you do, but I would still record in committee notes that Cao and Fatemi fall outside the three names, so that the omission is a conscious consequence of the limit and not an oversight. I also support your acceptance that a three-person B001 closes the door to a second part this year.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept that the unresolved pairing mechanism does not affect timeliness, given that Kroll, Lindroth and Johansson have raised it.
Whether the experimental credit, with Jarillo-Herrero as the only experimental name and Cao, Fatemi and others outside, will be seen as fair; I cannot resolve this from the supplied names.
How much weight earlier twisted-graphene band-structure theory deserves in the wording of the citation.
Whether B007 should be preferred if the committee weights maturity and clean attribution above field-opening novelty; I regard this as a difference of weighting, not of evidence.
My recollection of the latest clock uncertainty figures and of the formal timetable for the SI redefinition is from memory, not checked sources.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My profile documents no personal or institutional tie to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer, nor to Katori or Ye. I work in theoretical condensed-matter and electronic-structure physics, which is close to B001 in field but not in any documented collaboration. I note the disclosures of Kroll (Hall laboratory and JILA, relevant to B007), Johansson (B058) and Olsson (B030 and a possible Tokyo link to B007), and none of them affects my preferred configuration.
